title: feat(connector-mcp,spec): toolsSnapshot pins each MCP tool; a mismatch degrades through CONNECTOR_UPSTREAM_CHANGED
body:
Fixes #27401
Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: added
Skills-docs: follow-up owed — skills/** is not edited here (Tier H); whether a published skill should teach `providerConfig.toolsSnapshot` is for the seat that owns skills/**

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：MCP 连接器实例可以写 `providerConfig.toolsSnapshot`，按工具名逐个钉住工具定义的 sha256；服务端改写了被钉的工具（描述或参数）或不再提供它，实例进入降级、不暴露任何工具，原因里点名是哪个工具。降级走新错误码 `CONNECTOR_UPSTREAM_CHANGED`，日志写「工具定义与 toolsSnapshot 不符、退避重查」，不再借用「上游不可达」。
- 为什么改：执行你裁的两件事：逐工具钉快照（6506797088，B）和钉子不符要有自己的错误码与措辞（6545635244，B）。`CONNECTOR_UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` 仍只表示上游连不上。
- 风险与回滚：不写 `toolsSnapshot` 的实例行为完全不变；新错误码只有 connector-mcp 抛。回滚就是 revert 本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts`（新的降级分支和 ERROR 措辞）、`packages/spec/src/integration/connector-provider-errors.ts`（新错误类和判定函数）、`packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-provider.ts`（`toolsSnapshotDriftError`）。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-automation exec vitest run src/connector-upstream-changed.test.ts`，预期 5 个测试全过，其中一条断言 ERROR 原文是「serves a tool definition that differs from its toolsSnapshot … re-checking with backoff, attempt 1.」。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地（落地前要一次 `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` 契约复核，PM 安排）。

## What changes

Two rulings on this card, both letter B: the per-tool pin (comment 6506797088) and its own degrade marker (comment 6545635244). This PR picks up the branch's ruled connector-mcp work (head `68d8770f`) and merges `origin/main` into it.

**`@objectstack/connector-mcp`** (minor): `providerConfig.toolsSnapshot` on a `provider: 'mcp'` instance is a record of tool name → sha256 (lowercase hex) of the canonical JSON (RFC 8785 form) of the tool's `{ name, description, inputSchema }`. `computeMcpToolsSnapshot` and `mcpToolDigest` are exported.
- Refused before connecting, as plain configuration faults (fatal at boot): a malformed record, and a pin on a tool `include` leaves out (such a pin could never be checked).
- After `tools/list`, each pinned tool is compared on its own. If a pinned tool changed, or the server no longer serves it, the client is closed and the factory throws **`ConnectorUpstreamChangedError`**. Its one-line message names each such tool and the digest the server now serves.
- When the server stops serving a pinned tool that `include` also lists, the pin reports it. It is not reported as an `include` typo.

**`@objectstack/spec`** (patch, new code ⇒ `Clause-②: yes (widening)`): `CONNECTOR_UPSTREAM_CHANGED`, `ConnectorUpstreamChangedError`, and the structural guard `isConnectorUpstreamChanged`, which reads `code` and never uses `instanceof`. They are declared beside the outage and credential-rejected markers in `integration/connector-provider-errors.ts`. Its row sits in `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER` under `@objectstack/spec` (`door: 'none'`). The `ConnectorProviderFactory` TSDoc names it as a degrading marker. The header block of that file is left alone because open PR #28357 edits it.

**`@objectstack/service-automation`** (patch): this is the one materializer branch the ruling asks for. `isConnectorUpstreamChanged(thrown)` calls `degradeConnectorInstance` with `fault: 'changed'`. The backoff is the same 5 s → 5 min as an outage, and the husk's reason is the provider's message. Only the wording differs:
- Materializer ERROR: `… (provider 'P') serves a tool definition that differs from its toolsSnapshot — instance registered degraded (no actions); re-checking with backoff, attempt N.`
- Engine degrade WARN (`registerDegradedConnector`, which reads the same structural guard on the `cause` it already receives, with no signature change): `… no actions and no handlers until its upstream serves the definitions its pin names again; … the materializer re-checks with backoff.`

`CONNECTOR_UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` keeps its declared meaning and its wording. A control test pins that.

Docs: `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx` (the key's section and the fault table row). Generated: `api-surface/integration.json`, `export-origins/integration.json`, and three `content/docs/references/api/*` pages, written by `check:generated --fix`.

## Acceptance notes

- **The hasLive case keeps the outage policy.** Suppose an instance is already serving and its declaration is edited while the server has drifted from the new pin. The previously materialized connector keeps serving, and the ERROR says so. This is the same as an unreachable upstream on an edit, and the same backoff swaps it in on recovery. The ruling asked for "the same backoff", and nothing here takes a live connector down.
- **The ERROR wording names `toolsSnapshot`.** That follows the ruling's quoted text. The marker itself is provider-neutral, and mcp is its only producer today. A future provider pinning something else would need its own wording.
- The connector-mcp changeset predates this round and carries the two declaration lines. The spec and service-automation changesets declare `Metadata-protocol: none` (an error code and a log wording; no author-writable key), so they ship `patch`. connector-mcp ships `minor` for `added`.
